title: Gender-specific mortality in DTP-IPV- and MMR±MenC-eligible age groups to determine possible sex-differential effects of vaccination: an observational study.
ehr_evidence: The data were available from Statistics Netherlands, who linked demographic data of persons included in the Municipal Personal Records Database (GBA) with causes of death derived from Statistics Netherlands.
summary: Observational study of gender-specific mortality among Dutch children aged 0-11 years (2000-2011) to assess sex-differential effects of DTP-IPV and MMR ± MenC vaccinations.
key_findings: Mortality rate for natural causes was higher among boys than girls in all age groups.
Adjusted IRRs for girls compared with boys ranged between 0.81 (95% CI 0.74-0.89) and 0.91 (95% CI 0.77-1.07) across age groups.
No statistically significant differences in IRRs were observed between vaccine-related age groups (p = 0.723, p = 0.493, p = 0.868).
Sensitivity analyses including only indigenous Dutch children, specific death categories, and time periods yielded no statistically significant differences in IRR between vaccine-related age groups.
pathologies_diseases: diseases of the nervous, circulatory, and respiratory systems
population: all Dutch children aged 0-11 years from 2000 to 2011 (N=6,261,472)
exposure_domain: routine childhood vaccinations (DTP-IPV, MMR ± MenC, and boosters)
limitations: individual vaccination status could not be verified and was assumed based on national schedule
changes in vaccination schedule during the study period
low overall childhood mortality limits statistical power to detect non-specific effects
BCG vaccination for specific subgroups could interfere with results
